scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: CRM dispute ticket response times (2,440 tickets) show median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-03.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1,240 ESTIMATED and 1,785 ACTUAL (total 3,025), with ACTUAL-read bills forming the majority of disputes.

F-04.statement: The billing-db tariff_change_log contains zero records for the review period, i.e. no tariff change was logged.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-SLOW-RESPONSE-AUTOMATION-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is mainly a response-handling problem: tickets pile up because answers/corrections aren't automated, so an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes bills would resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE-MISVALIDATION.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules (logged in DA-RULES) around August altered which reads are accepted, increasing estimate substitution and producing incorrect bills.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI interval reads are failing to deliver or validate correctly through the nightly H-MDMS-BILL export, so billing lacks accepted reads and substitutes estimates, causing wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter reads from MeterWorks are not reaching billing correctly (H-FIELD-BILL) or route completion dropped, causing missed reads and estimate substitution; SH-FIELD's staffing narrative may itself be a self-serving alternative framing.

H-NONBILLING-DISPUTE-DRIVER.statement: Bills are largely accurate but disputes rose because of a non-error change (e.g., tariff, estimate policy, or billing cycle shift) that customers perceive as wrong, rather than a true read/import defect.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log record shows manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 ran at 88%, seven points below the 95% target, across 9200 manual-read accounts, indicating a measurable shortfall in field read collection during the dispute-surge window.

The observation shows CRM dispute ticket response times (2,440 tickets, median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are already within the 3.0-day SLA, indicating the dispute surge is not primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem as the requester's framing suggests.

The billing-db disputed_bills_by_read_type query (E-03) shows 1,785 of 3,025 disputed bills (59%) are ACTUAL-read bills versus 1,240 (41%) ESTIMATED-read bills, meaning disputes are not predominantly tied to estimate substitution and most disputed bills were built from reads that were actually received, not estimated.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records, meaning no tariff change was logged in the system of record during the review period. This rules out a tariff change as the mechanism behind the "non-error" explanation of the dispute surge.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims manual-read routes have run late since July due to being short three readers, and that affected customers receive estimated bills as a result; this is an unverified stakeholder claim offering a causal mechanism for the route-completion shortfall already observed in E-01, not new tool evidence. SH-FIELD's stated incentive (contract headcount increase) and documented bias (attributes problems to staffing) mean this narrative needs independent corroboration before being treated as established cause.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states no tariff change occurred this year; this stakeholder claim corroborates E-04's authoritative tool finding of zero tariff-change-log records, further weakening a tariff-change explanation for the dispute surge.

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly shows disputes at ~600/month in June-July 2026 (610, 590) rising to 1180-1260/month in August-September 2026, numerically confirming the stakeholder-reported doubling. The surge onset is August, one month after SH-FIELD's claimed staffing shortage "since July," since July volume (590) is not elevated relative to June (610).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract document confirms that the utility may request field route priority changes, but any such change (push_route_update) is executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) — matching the already-recorded K-DISPATCH constraint rather than revealing a new causal fact.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.question: What is causing the 59% majority of disputed bills that used ACTUAL reads (not ESTIMATED) to be disputed?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.decision_impact: If the actual-read dispute driver differs from the route-completion/estimate mechanism, remediation scope changes substantially and no bill-correcting action should be taken until it is identified.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.resolution_path: Disaggregate billing-db disputed_bills_by_read_type by dispute reason code, meter type, and billing-config rule version to find what the ACTUAL-read disputed bills have in common.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Continue read-only analyze_actual_read_disputes diagnostics only; report affected accounts for Billing Operations' own manual review under K-BILLWRITE rather than any automated fix.

U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.question: Is the manual-read route-completion shortfall actually caused by the field staffing shortage SH-FIELD claims (E-05), or by another cause such as a field-to-billing handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) delivery failure?
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: The root cause determines whether the fix is a route-priority push to SH-FIELD or a handoff/pipeline repair; pushing a route update before this is known risks acting on the wrong lever.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Cross-reference route-log completion records with H-FIELD-BILL handoff delivery/semantic-validity status and MeterWorks staffing data for Aug-Sep to see whether missed routes correlate with staffing gaps or handoff failures.
U-ROUTE-COMPLETION-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Run only read-only verify_route_completion_cause and check_field_billing_handoff diagnostics; do not execute push_route_update until the mechanism is confirmed and K-DISPATCH runtime confirmation is sought.

U-BASELINE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.question: Is the Jun-Jul (~600/month) dispute volume a valid pre-surge baseline, or could seasonal/other factors affect the apparent doubling?
U-BASELINE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.decision_impact: If the baseline is not representative, the SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE target and the measured size of the 'surge' would need revision.
U-BASELINE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.resolution_path: Pull crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly for the equivalent Jun-Sep window in prior year(s) to check for a recurring seasonal pattern before treating 600/month as fixed.
U-BASELINE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.safe_placeholder: Use the observed 600/month Jun-Jul figure as a provisional working baseline for SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-BASELINE while flagging it as unconfirmed pending year-over-year comparison.

A-ROUTE-SHORTFALL-LINKS-DISPUT.statement: The accounts affected by the Aug-Sep manual-read route-completion shortfall are assumed to overlap with the accounts generating dispute tickets, though no evidence record directly joins route-log accounts to disputing accounts.

A-STAFFING-CAUSES-SHORTFALL.statement: SH-FIELD's claim that a staffing shortage since July explains the route-completion drop is treated as a plausible lead, but it is an unverified, potentially self-interested stakeholder account.

A-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-APPLIE.statement: The meter-to-cash process is assumed to actually substitute estimates for missed manual reads as documented in its step list, driving the ESTIMATED-read disputes counted in E-03.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,200-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07).
Manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-01).

problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,200-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026, E-07), with the surge onset coinciding with manual-read route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep (E-01). Missed manual reads trigger estimate substitution in the billing-import step of the meter-to-cash process, and estimated bills are a documented driver of disputes (1,240 of 3,025 disputed bills, 41%, are ESTIMATED-read, E-03), making the manual-read route-completion shortfall the best-evidenced contributing cause of the dispute surge among the hypotheses tested. This mechanism does not account for the ACTUAL-read majority of disputed bills (59%, E-03), which remains an open question, and ticket response times are already within the 3.0-day SLA (E-02), ruling out the requester's response-automation framing as the fix.
